newsitem.title: USA: U.S. agency encourages more breast-feeding.
newsitem.headline: U.S. agency encourages more breast-feeding.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department began a year-long project Wednesday to encourage more mothers to breast-feed their babies.
"The idea here...is to raise awareness and public support for breast-feeding," Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said during a ceremony at Children's Hospital to launch the programme.
About 50 percent of U.S. children are breast-fed in the hospital after birth but the rate declines once they get home.

Goals of the department's project include wider public acceptance of breast-feeding and, through a special food programme for low income families, to encourage new mothers to breast-feed infants and make it easier for them to do so.
"We are going to eliminate that stigma" of embarrassment and lack of support from family and friends that deters women from breast-feeding, Undersecretary Shirley Watkins said.
